questions.q: Why isn't a gate set consisting only of transversal Clifford gates (X, Z, H, CNOT) enough for universal quantum computation?
options: The Gottesman-Knill theorem shows Clifford-only circuits can be efficiently simulated classically, providing no quantum advantage
Clifford gates cannot be implemented on any real quantum hardware
Clifford gates are not actually transversal on any known code
Universal quantum computation requires at least 20 different gate types
questions.explain: Gottesman-Knill is the well-established reason a Clifford-only quantum computer is classically simulable and thus not useful for quantum advantage -- at least one non-Clifford gate is required.

questions.q: Why is the T gate a problem for codes like the Steane code and surface code, despite their other gates being transversal?
options: T generally cannot be implemented transversally on these codes at the fidelity needed for real fault-tolerant computation
The T gate does not exist as a valid quantum operation
T is actually a Clifford gate and poses no special challenge
T can only be applied to ancilla qubits, never to data qubits
questions.explain: Unlike X, Z, H, and CNOT, the T gate resists the cheap transversal-gate approach on these code families, which is exactly why a separate solution (magic-state distillation) is needed.

questions.q: What does the 15-to-1 magic-state distillation protocol do?
options: It consumes 15 noisy magic states and outputs 1 magic state of substantially higher fidelity
It consumes 1 magic state and produces 15 copies of equal fidelity
It converts 15 logical qubits into 1 physical qubit
It distills classical bits into quantum magic states
questions.explain: The 15-to-1 protocol is a well-known concrete example: 15 noisy inputs yield 1 higher-fidelity output magic state, usable via gate teleportation to apply a high-fidelity logical T gate.

questions.q: How is a distilled magic state actually used to apply a logical T gate to a computation?
options: Via gate teleportation, consuming the high-fidelity magic state to apply the logical T gate
By directly measuring the magic state and discarding the result
By applying it transversally, qubit by qubit, exactly like a Clifford gate
Magic states are purely theoretical and are never actually consumed by real circuits
questions.explain: Gate teleportation is the standard technique for consuming a distilled magic state to apply a high-fidelity logical T gate to the actual computation.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say magic-state distillation overhead is often a dominant, not minor, contributor to total resource cost?
options: It adds a separate, additional layer of physical qubits and operations on top of the base QEC overhead from chapter 6, purely to manufacture enough high-fidelity T gates
Magic-state distillation actually reduces the total qubit count needed below the base QEC overhead
Distillation overhead is always negligible and can be safely ignored in resource estimates
Distillation only matters for algorithms that use zero T gates
questions.explain: Distillation is additional overhead beyond the per-logical-qubit QEC cost from chapter 6, and in many detailed estimates (including the kind cited for Shor's algorithm) it is a major, sometimes dominant, contributor to total resource needs.
